thought_title: Disciples matched to sicknesses and Luke as physician
orientation: The preacher is still laying out why Christ chose Luke the physician alongside Peter, Matthew and Paul.
pass_a_gloss: to the authorities in the heavenly places through the church the very varied wisdom of God. And observe for me the wisdom of the master; from every knowledge and craft he chose for himself disciples, Peter from fishermen, Matthew from tax collectors, Paul from tent makers, Luke from physicians. And he did this not by chance nor simply; for the nature of human beings was in the depth of error and there was need of fishermen. Again the devil collected tax from Adam after he snatched away immortality; there was need of an evangelist who is a tax collector. Disobedience clothed the human being in the garments of skin; there was need of the tent maker and of grace, in order that he might cut through the deadening of the passions with the knife of the divine Word. The race of human beings was sick in varied ways, with fever of licentiousness, with envy of love of money and with pleasure, with despair of evil eye, with unreason of idolatry. For this reason he established Luke for them as a skilled physician and Paul cries out, “Luke the physician greets you”; for in truth Luke is a physician of souls. Do you wish to see his workshop? See heaven. Do you wish to see his place of healing? See his journey through the world. Do you wish to see his store of drugs? See the operating work on Jewish tongues. Do you wish to see his plants? See the various healings. Do you wish to see the sick whom he visits? See the heretics living nearby. For on the one side those who reject the Spirit are sick with blasphemy, and on the other side those who reject the Son are sick with godlessness, but to both as a physician he prescribes what is fitting, saying to the first, “Do not grieve the Holy Spirit,” and crying to the second, “He who does not honor the Son does not honor the Father either.” Truly Luke is a great physician. And do you wish to see his craft? See the divine Gospel; for the other evangelists made their narrative of one kind. What kind of thing I mean is this; Matthew began from the genealogy according to the flesh saying, “Book of generation of Jesus Christ son of David son of Abraham.” Mark also proclaimed the plan of salvation according to the flesh saying, “Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee.”

pass_b_english: “to the authorities in the heavenly places through the church the manifold wisdom of God” (Ephesians 3:10). Consider the wisdom of the Master. He chose his disciples for himself from every science and craft: Peter from fishermen, Matthew from tax collectors, Paul from tentmakers, and Luke from physicians. He did this not by chance and not without purpose. Humanity lay in the depth of error, and fishermen were needed. The devil had taxed Adam and robbed him of immortality, and an evangelist who was a tax collector was needed. Disobedience had clothed mankind in tunics of skin, and a tentmaker was needed, with grace to cut away the deadness of the passions with the knife of the divine Word.

The human race lay sick with many diseases: with the fever of debauchery, with the envy of greed and pleasure, with the despair that comes from the evil eye, and with the folly of idolatry. So Christ set Luke over them as a proven physician, and Paul cries out, “Luke the physician greets you” (Colossians 4:14). For Luke is truly a physician of souls. Do you want to see his workshop? Look at heaven. Do you want to see his practice? Look at his journey through the whole world. Do you want to see his store of drugs? Look at his surgery on Jewish tongues. Do you want to see his healing herbs? Look at the many different cures. Do you want to see the sick whom he visits? Look at the heretics next door. On one side those who reject the Spirit are sick with blasphemy, and on the other those who reject the Son are diseased with denial of God. Yet to both he prescribes what each needs, as a physician should. To the first Luke says, “Do not grieve the Holy Spirit” (Ephesians 4:30), and to the second he cries, “Whoever does not honor the Son does not honor the Father” (John 5:23). Luke is truly a great physician.

Do you want to see his skill? Look at the divine Gospel. The other evangelists told their story in one manner. What I mean is this. Matthew began from the genealogy according to the flesh, saying, “The book of the genealogy of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham” (Matthew 1:1). Mark also proclaimed the plan of salvation according to the flesh, saying, “Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee” (Mark 1:9).
